title: The Number That Comes Up
logline: At a dry-zone town junction, a lottery-ticket seller's daily calling turns into a private ritual for regulars who buy the same numbers morning after morning, certain today might finally be the day.

object.note: Object 2 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Patient effort that expects a result gives way to its opposite: a daily ritual of buying the same numbers, wanting without quite expecting.

thread_out.thread: The daily hope at the lottery kiosk becomes a wait in a station ticket queue, where the board changes just before one traveller's turn.

requirements: An active ticket kiosk with a willing seller
Regular customers willing to speak about their habit
A working evening draw broadcast on site

suggestions.name: A bus-stand or town-junction kiosk in Anuradhapura
suggestions.why: A well-known dry-zone town with an active bus stand and daily lottery trade.
suggestions.verify: No seller has been contacted; exact kiosk and willingness to be filmed are unverified.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.
